newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Farmers rethink switch.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Farmers rethink switch.

text.p: Spring wheat prices continued to rise on Friday, prompting farmers to begin to rethink plans to switch acreage from spring wheat to soybeans this year, particularly in North Dakota, grain dealers said.
"People who were thinking of switching will probably switch back to wheat now," one grain dealer said.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture's March planting survey forecast a 20 percent cut in North Dakota's hard red spring wheat acreage to 7.7 million acres.
Soybean acres in the state were seen rising 35 percent to 1.1 million.
Plantings in North Dakota were reported to be off to a slow start amid heavy flooding in the Red River valley.
"Hopefully the worst of the flooding is behind us, but we're not sure. There is still a lot of water out there," one North Dakota dealer said.
In Montana spring wheat plantings were seen gathering pace next week.
